subject: Cedarway + Redwood: solution validation and acceptance
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cedarway.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cedarway + Redwood: reference design validation and acceptance

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Cedarway is excited to move forward with a partner reference integration that we can showcase to a few of our enterprise customers. Before we commit to a public joint reference, we need a short technical validation cycle to confirm the solution architecture, performance targets, and operational controls.

What we'd like to validate during a 3-day lab run:
- Basic API compatibility (Redwood hosted and Dedicated endpoints)
- VPC peering + Private control plane connectivity for our staging VPC
- Latency profile for our common request shapes (prompt lengths 64, 512, 2048 tokens)
- Robustness of fallback behavior when a Dedicated pool is constrained
- Security evidence (SOC2 artifact pointer, audit log delivery for queries)

I've attached a short spec that outlines our expected test cases (cedarway-integration-specs.pdf). Proposed dates: Nov 30 - Dec 2. Can Redwood provide a dedicated test pool or guidance on capacity we should reserve? Also please confirm an internal owner for the run and the acceptance criteria you'll use to sign off.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Partnerships
Cedarway Systems

Attachment: cedarway-integration-specs.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cedarway.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cedarway + Redwood: reference design validation and acceptance

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the clear spec — this looks straightforward. We're available to run the 3-day lab Nov 30–Dec 2. We'll do the following on our side:
- Stand up a short-lived Dedicated pool (3 x A100 equivalent) with test routing to your workspace
- Provide a Private staging plan if you want VPC peering and a customer-managed control plane
- Run latency/throughput sweeps for your token shapes and produce percentile metrics (p50/p95/p99)
- Execute failure injection to validate our fallback to hosted variants and rollout policies

I've attached our initial interop checklist (redwood-interop-checklist.xlsx) — it includes the acceptance gates we typically use. For signoff we propose these primary acceptance criteria:
1) Functional parity: no API surface mismatches for basic generation and chat flows
2) Performance: p50 < 120ms for short prompts (64 tokens), p95 < 300ms for mid-length (512), p99 < 800ms for long (>=2048) under your baseline load
3) Reliability: graceful fallback in >=95% of injected constrained scenarios
4) Security: audit logs and event streams delivered to your audit collector in near-real-time

Internal owner from Redwood: I'll serve as technical lead; Marissa will own project coordination. Sergio will help on capacity configuration and runbook.

Can you share the staging AWS account IDs and a preferred Slack channel so we can provision access?

Thanks — I'll schedule a short pre-run call for Thursday to confirm the runbook.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-interop-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cedarway.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cedarway + Redwood: solution validation and acceptance

Elena / team —

Run complete; summary and signoff below. Full raw results and the acceptance-test-results-summary.csv are in the shared Drive link. Highlights:
- Functional parity: Pass (generation and chat API surfaces matched; one minor header mismatch, patched)
- Performance: All primary targets met under Cedarway's baseline load. Observed percentiles: short prompts p50=85ms p95=210ms p99=430ms; mid prompts p50=170ms p95=420ms p99=870ms; long prompts p50=620ms p95=1.2s p99=2.3s (long-tail expected at very high token counts)
- Reliability: Fallback behavior exercised via controlled pod preemption — success rate 96.8% for graceful reroute to hosted variant
- Security: Audit events forwarded to Cedarway audit collector within 45s on average; SOC2 evidence pointers in Drive

Open items:
- We saw p99 spikes for very long prompts under simultaneous burst; recommend a quantized candidate (8-bit) for the long-prompt offering and a small caching window for repetitive prefixes.
- Marketing collateral: Marissa, please confirm the short-form acceptance blurb we'll publish.

DocuSign SOW link recorded as executed by Cedarway procurement; HubSpot deal HS-48392 updated with results. Attaching the summarized CSV: acceptance-test-results-summary.csv

If Cedarway agrees these acceptance gates are met, Redwood signs off on the reference validation and we can schedule a joint PR/tech talk.

Thanks everyone — great collaboration.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acceptance-test-results-summary.csv (CSV, 18KB)
